Privacy Wiki

What they collect. Why it matters. How to turn it off.

A plain account of how consumer platforms collect, share, and monetize your data, and the exact steps to limit it. Written from the inside.

Platforms

All platforms →

One page per company. What they collect, which settings matter, and how to turn them off.

  • TikTok Off-platform tracking via TikTok Pixel, GPS collection added in 2026, no AI training opt-out for US users.
  • X / Twitter Default-on Grok AI training added in 2024, data sharing with unspecified business partners, cross-device targeting.
  • Meta / Instagram The Meta Pixel tracks you across millions of third-party websites. Off-Facebook Activity, Audience Network ads, AI training with no US opt-out.
  • Google Google Analytics and the Google Ads network reach roughly 90% of top websites. Cross-product data from Search, YouTube, Maps, Gmail, Chrome, and Android.
  • Amazon Purchase history, Alexa voice recordings, Ring footage, cross-site ad network, and Amazon One palm biometrics. A household-level behavioral profile.
  • YouTube A Google product. Watch history, search queries, and granular engagement data feed the same Google advertising profile used across Search, Gmail, and the Display Network.

Practices

All practices →

One page per data collection technique. How it works across every platform that uses it.

  • Off-Platform Activity Tracking When you close the app, the tracking does not stop. How platforms monitor behavior across the rest of the internet.
  • AI Training Data Usage Most platforms are using your content to train AI models by default. Opt-outs are forward-looking only.
  • Ad Personalization and Targeting Turning off personalized ads does not stop data collection. What the toggle actually controls.
  • Third-Party Data Sharing Platforms share your data with companies you have never interacted with. What leaves the platform and where it goes.
  • Data Brokers Profiles built from public records, purchase history, and behavioral data — sold without your involvement. Opt-outs are piecemeal.
  • Location Data Your location is collected continuously, sold by data brokers, and purchased by advertisers and government agencies. A location history reveals home, workplace, and medical visits.
  • Dark Patterns Deliberate interface design that makes consent frictionless and opt-out hard. The toggle exists; it is just buried, grayed out, and three submenus away.

Built by someone who works in ad tech. Verified against live settings, not marketing copy.
